decisive_items: symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6; ST-segment depression in leads aVR and aVL
response.rationale: Antecedent URI, high troponin, diffuse ST elevation with low voltage, and normal coronaries with multifocal LV dysfunction are classic for acute myocarditis; high procalcitonin suggests systemic inflammation but does not override the ECG/echo pattern.

rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries and diffuse ST elevation/low voltage argue against acute coronary syndrome.
Lacks the infectious prodrome and procalcitonin elevation; stress cardiomyopathy is less consistent with the diffuse ECG changes and young age.
Sepsis alone does not explain severe LV dysfunction, diffuse ST elevation, or the marked troponin/BNP elevation.
